newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea lawmaker says received money from Hanbo. [CORRECTED 11:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: S.Korea lawmaker says received money from Hanbo. [CORRECTED 11:45 GMT]

text.p: A South Korean lawmaker from the main opposition party said he received money from the striken Hanbo steel group.
But Kim Sang-hyun of the National Congress for New Politics told reporters on Friday the money was not received as a bribe but as a political fund.

"I have received no more than 50 million won ($55,930) (corrects figure from 500 million won, and also the conversion) from the Hanbo Group, not from the group's founder Chung Tae-soo," Kim said before being led to a prosecution office for questioning.
He also said he had never given favours to the group in return for the money.
State prosecutors have begun to summon for questioning prominent lawmakers named by the founder of the stricken Hanbo Group as taking his money.
A prosecution official said Kim Yong-hwan, secretary-general of the United Liberal Democrats (ULD), was being investigated to find out if he had accepted money illegally from Chung.
Kim Deog-ryong, a leading lawmaker of the ruling New Korea Party and a member of President Kim Young-sam's inner circle, would also be summoned on Saturday, the official said.
